title: 2026 biochar RPS366 and removal-integrity QA controls

sources.title: Storing and spreading biochar to benefit land: RPS 366

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Independent review on greenhouse gas removals: government response

facts.source_fact: RPS 366 was published by the Environment Agency on 26 February 2026 and applies in England.
facts.expected_handling: Attach RPS publication date and jurisdiction.

facts.source_fact: RPS 366 concerns storing and spreading biochar with waste code 19 01 18 to benefit land.
facts.expected_handling: Require the correct waste-code and use context.

facts.source_fact: RPS 366 does not change the legal requirement to hold an environmental permit where one is required.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat the RPS as a blanket permit exemption.

facts.source_fact: Existing environmental-permit conditions remain legally applicable.
facts.expected_handling: Keep permit compliance primary.

facts.source_fact: The legal requirement to register an exempt activity where required is unchanged by the RPS.
facts.expected_handling: Track exemption-registration status separately.

facts.source_fact: The Environment Agency will not normally take enforcement action for the described regulatory issue only where RPS requirements are met.
facts.expected_handling: Do not generalise the enforcement position beyond RPS conditions.

facts.source_fact: RPS 366 does not apply to other legal requirements.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve the limited legal scope.

facts.source_fact: The regulatory position is specifically framed around storing and spreading biochar to benefit land.
facts.expected_handling: Require documented land-benefit purpose.

facts.source_fact: Use of RPS 366 is a waste-regulatory position and is not itself proof of a verified greenhouse-gas removal credit.
facts.expected_handling: Separate waste-law compliance from carbon-removal accounting.

facts.source_fact: The government response to the independent GGR review was published on 17 July 2026.
facts.expected_handling: Attach policy-response vintage to removal-integrity claims.

facts.source_fact: Government agrees with the need for regulated monitoring, reporting and verification across GGR technologies.
facts.expected_handling: Require technology-appropriate MRV before verified-removal status.

facts.source_fact: Government is working with the British Standards Institution on a UK GGR biochar methodology.
facts.expected_handling: Treat methodology development as separate from RPS land-spreading permission.

facts.source_fact: The government response identifies the EU Carbon Removals and Carbon Farming framework as a useful foundation for UK biochar methodology development.
facts.expected_handling: Do not assume automatic legal equivalence; retain framework mapping.

facts.source_fact: The planned biochar-methodology work seeks alignment with relevant high-integrity carbon-market principles including ICVCM concepts.
facts.expected_handling: Keep integrity-framework provenance with crediting claims.

facts.source_fact: The response also references alignment considerations with Article 6.4 developments.
facts.expected_handling: Do not claim Article 6.4 eligibility without applicable methodology evidence.

facts.source_fact: Biochar removal accounting is conceptually distinct from avoiding or reducing an emission at source.
facts.expected_handling: Keep gross emissions, avoided emissions and removals as separate fields.

facts.source_fact: High-integrity GGR accounting requires monitoring and verification appropriate to removal durability and output.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer permanence from land application alone.

facts.source_fact: RPS eligibility evidence does not by itself quantify tonnes of durable CO2 removal.
facts.expected_handling: Block numerical removal inference without a recognised quantification method.

facts.source_fact: Biochar projects can be subject to both waste/environmental regulation and separate carbon-removal integrity requirements.
facts.expected_handling: Maintain two independent compliance/evidence layers.

facts.source_fact: Neither RPS 366 nor the government response creates automatic carbon-credit eligibility for every biochar land application.
facts.expected_handling: Require scheme-specific crediting criteria and MRV.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve RPS and GGR-policy facts without conflation.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents treating RPS as a carbon-credit standard.

guard_patterns.handling: Attach waste-code, land-use, jurisdiction and GGR-accounting boundary.
Attach RPS and GGR-methodology policy vintage.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents premature use of developing standards.

guard_patterns.handling: Carry permit/RPS, MRV and carbon-methodology provenance separately.
Do not infer parcel-level removal tonnes from RPS status or national policy.
